result.title: Optimizing Recourse Under Predictive Multiplicity
result.summary: Algorithmic recourse identifies modifications that can change an unfavorable model prediction into a favorable one. Under predictive multiplicity, similarly performing models can disagree on individual predictions, so recourse valid for one model may fail for another. We formulate robust recourse under predictive multiplicity as a budget-constrained minimization of the worst-case validity loss across a competing set of models, which can include models with different architectures or from different hypothesis classes. We propose an oracle-efficient algorithm called ORPM and prove sufficient conditions for its convergence. We evaluate ORPM on one synthetic and five real datasets, and competing sets consist of linear, neural, mixed, and decision-tree models. Our experiments show decreasing optimization-gap bounds and high validity in many tested settings, with favorable performance against baselines designed for specific model classes or architectures. We also quantify how requiring a common action across competing models changes recourse success at a given budget and examine disparities in this success across demographic groups.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究预测多重性（predictive multiplicity）下算法追索的稳健性，将跨竞争模型集合的最坏情况有效性损失表述为预算约束下的最小化问题，提出 oracle-efficient 算法 ORPM 并给出收敛条件，在多类模型组成的竞争集合上评测，并量化要求共同动作对成功率及群体差异的影响。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「竞争模型集合下预算约束的最坏情况优化」及不同模型对同一样本判断分歧的刻画，可能为多 latent 假设/多解码器聚合与有限计算预算下的假设筛选提供可核查的优化与评价线索，但领域相距较远，需人工判断可迁移性。
